data.cause: The primary DNS resolver on dns1.lan enforces a 20 q/s per-subnet rate limit and silently drops .lan (and other) queries whenever the 10.20.0.0/24 aggregate briefly exceeds it; retries then hit gw.lan's unbound, whose private-address rebinding protection also suppresses the local 10.20.0.50 answers for *.lan, so getaddrinfo sees ENOTFOUND until the burst passes a minute or two later.
evidence: journalctl -u primary-dns on dns1.lan shows repeated 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping N queries' events (02:14, 09:41, 13:02), each followed by 'back under limit' within seconds to ~30s — matching alerts that occur a few times a day and self-clear within a minute or two
cat /opt/primary-dns/config.yaml shows ratelimit: 20 with ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24 applied to all traffic including the local rewrites for *.lan / nas.lan -> 10.20.0.50
dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan normally returns 10.20.0.50 (NOERROR, ANSWER: 1), so the zone data itself is fine; failures only coincide with rate-limit drops

dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan returns NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 (empty answer) — gw.lan's unbound forwards lan. to 10.20.0.3 but its private-address: 10.0.0.0/8 rebinding filter strips the private answer, so the client's second server cannot rescue local names either
/etc/resolv.conf on mon.lan lists 10.20.0.3 then 10.20.0.1, confirming clients fall back to gw.lan when dns1 drops their query
data.recommendation: Raise or remove the overly aggressive ratelimit on dns1.lan's primary-dns (e.g., increase it well above normal aggregate LAN traffic, or exempt the locally rewritten .lan zones from rate limiting). Additionally, fix gw.lan's fallback path so the backup resolver can still serve local names during a burst: declare lan. as authoritative/local in unbound (or exclude the forwarded lan. zone from the private-address filtering) so that private answers for *.lan are not stripped. The smallest action that fixes the intermittent ENOTFOUND is adjusting the ratelimit setting on dns1; correcting gw.lan's config makes the configured second DNS server actually usable for local names.
data.detail: primary-dns ratelimit of 20 q/s per /24 drops LAN queries during traffic bursts
